tweets.text:
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. quoted.text: I stopped using Claude about two weeks ago because it was becoming increasingly difficult/combative/manipulative to work with. Switched to Grok Bot as a test run for repeated tasks and had it scan my computers for regular file clean up. It found 22+ GBs of temp files, and bloat from Claude that I had no idea existed even though I had a daily task set up for Claude to scan my disk for file organization, space usage, and recommend deletions. It never flagged this or told me it created a virtual Linux computer for agent work. If you’re using Claude desktop, check your disk space, and if it looks unreasonably full, have another LLM scan your hard to see why.

quoted.text: Grok Build just got a solid upgrade for headless agents, MCP integrations, and remote terminal workflows Headless sessions can now include images returned by MCP tools in streaming and JSON output, positional prompts automatically run headless when no interactive terminal is available, and local file links open directly from responses Long-running headless tasks also get better reliability, with a five-minute inactivity timeout that prevents sessions from hanging indefinitely. Image pasting now works through remote tmux and nested terminal wrappers, while session recovery and hook inspection are more dependable There’s also a performance improvement that eliminates unnecessary directory watching when Grok only needs to track the current Git branch Release Notes: v1.0.92 Features: • Positional prompts without `-p` now run headless and print their reply when the process has no terminal for the TUI • MCP tool results that contain images now include those images in headless streaming and JSON output • Clickable `file://` links to local files now open the file the same way bare paths do Bug Fixes: • Question cards in minimal mode now keep the first option visible instead of scrolling it off-screen • Headless runs (`grok -p`) now stop after 5 minutes of no model output instead of hanging indefinitely • Session resume errors now give the same helpful instruction on every route instead of suggesting the TUI picker • `grok inspect` now shows the hooks a headless run would actually load, with a note for those that still need folder trust • Image paste with `grok wrap` now works when Grok runs inside a remote tmux or through a second wrap Performance: • Grok no longer watches every directory when only tracking the current Git branch
